horses.spotlight_comment: This looks to be in ideal opportunity for FINAL APPEAL to get off the mark after his promising second on his debut where he had Blackberry Bold just behind him. The main danger is Noble Raider, with the yard having their first juvenile winner of the season here earlier this month. [Andrew Bladen] Page 1 spotlightwolverhampton 21.04.26

All six have yet to win but the one that is knocking on the door is CROWN INN TO WIN who has finished runner-up on his last two starts. He is selected ahead of Corduroy who was third in a similar race here last time and has since changed yards. It's unusual for the Gosdens to have a runner a this low level and there may be more to come from Itsonlyrockandroll on her handicap debut. Forever Perfect was third in a similar race last time and may not be far away. [Andrew Bladen] Page 2 spotlightwolverhampton 21.04.26

Tony Carroll's likeable mare Midnight Call merits respect, even though she's raised in grade and 9lb higher than when winning stylishly over C&D a fortnight ago. However, preference is for the ultra-consistent SHALAA ASKER, who didn't have the cards fall his way when a close second here last time. [Mark Rowntree] Page 3 spotlightwolverhampton 21.04.26

The in-form BEAUNE (nap) is hard to get away from and he can cope with the 5lb rise for winning over C&D last time. The one to chase him home could be Rubellite who has six wins to her name and ran well when second for her new trainer last time. Wave Rock would hold claims over this new distance if she settles, while another to consider is Knight Of Magic. [Andrew Bladen] Page 4 spotlightwolverhampton 21.04.26

With the pacy Filly Foden and recent 5f fillies maiden winner Star Marian likely to take each other on for the lead, this could go the way of a late finisher and Ruth Carr's DAYTONA LADY fits the bill. She's nicely weighted and posted a fair recent comeback run at Southwell. [Mark Rowntree] Page 5 spotlightwolverhampton 21.04.26

This race may revolve around whether FASTER BEE can grab the lead, and if he does he could be difficult to peg back. Sanditon has disappointed since winning at Chelmsford two months ago but the handicapper has given him a chance and he is not out of this. Nor is Diligent Henry whose two wins have been over C&D and is down to his last winning mark. [Andrew Bladen] Page 6 spotlightwolverhampton 21.04.26

However, Ruth Carr's BAD HABITS had been knocking at the door until a blip (raced keenly) here last time, so it might pay to give him another chance. [Mark Rowntree] Page 7 spotlightwolverhampton 21.04.26

Dropping back to 9.4f should aid Eagles Whistle, while there were signs that Distinction (second choice) might be on the way back at Pontefract. However, the most obvious one is last-time winner KAARANAH, who responded positively to the introduction of cheekpieces over C&D a fortnight ago. [Mark Rowntree] Page 8
